thread:
maria: quick heads-up, ran a focused profile on host-side parse + gRPC stream for the long-chat workload. seeing ~30-40% CPU on tokenization + chunk framing when requests hit 1.2k tokens and streaming enabled :eyes:
aj: can you paste the flame or top samples?
maria: pasted flame snapshot (short):
```
Top nodes by CPU:
- host::tokenize (35%)
- host::frame_stream (18%)
- proto::unpack (12%)
- kvcache::check_hit (8%)
- kernel_select (7%)
```
This was with kernel hint="auto", batch target=16, kv hit ~62% (cold-ish).
aj: hmm 62% kv hit is low for chat. are we invalidating prefixes somewhere?
maria: not intentionally. trace shows lots of small fragments (100-300B) causing repeated parse paths + allocs. proto unpacks per-frag add up.
sam: that matches the microbench — small-fragment streaming causes O(n) overhead on framing. two quick ideas: reuse an arena for proto unpack, and coalesce small writes at ingress so parse sees fewer, bigger frames.
maría: (typo was accidental) I'll try the arena. also want to try forcing kernel hint to "smallseq" on these hosts to see if kernel_select overhead drops.
aj: also check kernel_select cost: if hint flips per-request it's adding branching. maybe compute hint once per-session and cache.
maria: good call. current code chooses kernel each request because seq_len distribution fluctuates. caching per-session + invalidation on long jump seems cheap to implement.
infra-bot: deploy v2-preflight to canary (host-pool-3) queued by maria — build 0.11.3-preflight.
aj: for batching heuristics: when kv hit < 70% we should bias towards smaller batch target to reduce wasted re-compute on misses. can we add a short-circuit in the scheduler?
maria: plan: add kv-hit sliding window (30s) to scheduler; if <70% set batch_target=8 and prefetch hot prefixes. will also flip streaming coalesce to 256B threshold.
nora: would love a concrete metric to track — request p95 latency, tokens/sec, and token CPU/sec. add an rr metric for kv-hit to Grafana.
maria: will add dashboards. early local run: arena + session-kernel-cache reduced parse allocs by ~42% and host CPU for tokenize down ~18% on a 1k token test. KV warmup improved to 78% after synthetic priming.
sam: awesome. next drop: grpc HTTP2 smallwrite overhead. can we enable writev coalesce on the ingress proxy for streams? that should reduce syscall churn.
aj: be careful: coalescing too aggressively increases tail latency for very interactive users. use adaptive coalesce: small-window coalesce but flush on end-of-chunk or 20ms.
maria: will prototype adaptive coalesce (20ms cap + max_coalesce_size=1kb). also testing writev on proxy in local.
infra-bot: canary deploy v2-preflight -> host-pool-3 succeeded in 2m.
aj: once canary runs for 30m, we should collect full traces and compare p50/p95 token-latency and CPU token/sec. can you post a diff? :thumbsup:
maria: will run 30m canary, collect traces and post results here. early signs look promising but want to validate burst patterns.
nora: assign follow-ups: maria -> implement arena + kernel-cache + coalesce prototype; aj -> scheduler kv-window + metric thresholds; sam -> proxy writev adaptive patch. add tickets and link in thread when created.
maria: created tickets: INF-4821, INF-4822, INF-4823. linking perf traces after canary.
aj: sounds good. thanks!
sam: LGTM.
